div.head: II Cn 12
div.ab: Ðis syndon þa gerihta, þe se cingc ah ofer ealle men on Wessexan: þæt is mundbryce ⁊ hamsocne, forsteal ⁊ flymena fyrmðe ⁊ fyrdwite, butan he hwæne ðe furðor gemæðrian wylle (⁊ he him ðæs weorðscipes geunne).
Þis syndon þa geriht, þe se cyningce ah ofer ealle menn [on] Westseaxan: þæt is mundbrice ⁊ hamsocne, forestal ⁊ fyrdigce, buton he hwæne furðor mæðrian wylle.

Hęc sunt iura, quę rex habet super omnes homines in Mircenis et Westsexa: mundbrece (id est infractionem pacis), hámsocnam (id est inuasionem mansionis), foresteal (id est prohibitionem itineris) et fyrdunga (id est expeditionem), nisi aliquem amplius honorare uelit.
Ðis syndon ða gerihta ðe se cyning ah ofer ealle men on Wessexan, þæt is mundbryce ⁊ hamsocne, forstal ⁊ fyrdwite, buton hwǽne he furðor gemæðian wylle.

Ðis syndon þa gerihta þe se cingc ah ofer ealle men on Wessexan: þæt is mundbryce and hamsocne, forsteal and flymena fyrmðe and fyrdwite, butan he hwæne ðe furðor gemæðrian wylle and he him ðæs weorðscipes geunne.

Dies sind die [Jurisdictions]gerechtsame, die der König über alle Leute in Wessex [vorbehalten] hat: nämlich den Bruch der [besonderen königlichen] Schutzgewalt und [unerlaubte] Heimsuchung, Wegsperrung (und Beherbergung Geächteter G) und Strafe für Heer[versäumniss], ausser wenn er jemanden (um so G) weiter ehren will (indem er ihm die Jurisdictionswürde [auch hierüber] verleiht G).

These are the [jurisdictional] rights which the king has [reserved] over all men in Wessex: namely breach of [his special] protection, and [unlawful] attack on a house, obstruction (and harbouring outlaws, G), and the fine for [neglect of] military service, unless he wishes to honour someone further (by granting him the jurisdiction [over these too], G).

These are the dues to which the king is entitled from all men in Wessex, namely, [the payments for] violation of his mund, and for attacks on people's houses, for assault and for neglecting military service, unless he desires to show especial honour to anyone [by granting him these dues].

These are the rights which the king possesses over all men in Wessex, namely mundbryce and hamsocn, forstal and [the fine for] the harbouring of fugitives and the fine for neglecting military service, unless he wishes to honour anyone further.

These are the fines to which the king is entitled from all the people of Wessex: that is, fines for the violation of the king’s protection and for home invasion, for assault, harboring of fugitives, and shirking military service, unless he wishes to specially privilege someone by allocating these fines to him.
div.note: G's ‘⁊ flymena fyrmðe’ is missing from the other MSS and not original; G's ‘ðe’ (also in 15) and ‘(⁊ he him ðæs weorðscipes geunne)’ are perhaps not original either (Liebermann). A's ‘fyrdigce’ should be ‘fyrdinge’. Quadr. includes Mercia (‘Mircenis’), drawn forward from 14.
This is mentioned only in the Nero version.
i.e. further than by giving the usual grant of private jurisdiction, which did not include these special royal pleas. The Nero version adds here: “and he grants him this privilege”.
